edges.description: Highly endocytic and phagocytic microglia accumulate enlarged or excess acidic lysosomal compartments.
Membrane trafficking defects in neurons are proposed to underlie the cerebellar atrophy; reduced Purkinje cell viability is plausible but not demonstrated.
Lysosomal and autophagic dysfunction is the proposed shared mechanism of dystonia across the HOPS-associated neurological disorders; the circuit-level route is not established.
Lysosomal accumulation impairs microglial function, and microglial loss is known to cause brain abnormalities including cerebellar hypoplasia; this contribution is proposed from the zebrafish data.
Cerebellar tissue loss is visible on MRI.
Nystagmus is a common cerebellar oculomotor sign; the specific substrate in SCAR29 has not been studied.
Microglial lysosomal accumulation rescued by wild-type vps41 mRNA.
edges.limitations: Mosaic F0 knockout rather than the patients' hypomorphic missense or splice alleles; larval stage only, and the microglial finding has not been examined in human tissue.

nodes.description: VPS41 is one of the two HOPS-specific subunits. All tested disease variants prevented formation of a functional HOPS complex. Because VPS41 is not part of CORVET, the defect is confined to the late endosome/autophagosome-to-lysosome fusion arm, in contrast to VPS33A (Mucopolysaccharidosis-Plus Syndrome), whose loss compromises both complexes. A HOPS-independent function of VPS41 in regulated secretion was preserved for the p.Ser285Pro allele.

nodes.description: Biallelic VPS41 variants reduce or abolish the function of the HOPS-specific VPS41 subunit. Disease missense variants fail to restore lysosomal function in VPS41 knockout cells, and in one compound heterozygote the two splice alleles (one producing an NMD-targeted out-of-frame transcript, one an in-frame exon-skipped transcript) jointly reduced VPS41 transcript and protein. VPS41 acts as an adaptor linking the HOPS complex to the lysosomal small GTPase ARL8B via its effector SKIP.

nodes.description: F0 crispants of the single zebrafish vps41 homologue show hypopigmentation, absent swim bladder inflation with loss of viability, increased brain lysosomal acidity concentrated in microglia, and a reduced optokinetic response.

In VPS41-deficient cells mTORC1 redistributes to the cytosol and TFE3 is continuously nuclear, while phosphorylation of the mTORC1 substrates S6K1 and 4EBP1 is unaffected; the defect is selective for the TFEB/TFE3 arm. Lysosomal biogenesis and autophagosome formation are continuously upregulated regardless of nutrient status, and the autophagic response to starvation is reduced.
